brief.input: Clean identified recycled rubber granules; pieces vary roughly between three and eight millimetres
brief.use_case: Indoor entry mat used in wet conditions
brief.targets: Good wet grip and easy cleaning; I have no numerical limits or readings
brief.variation: Some portions contain more large pieces and others more small pieces
brief.process: At home: hand tools, scissors and cool water. No press, heated equipment or laboratory.
brief.contamination: No identified contaminants; no contaminant test has been done
brief.available_changes: Can change the layout or product design, but cannot purchase extra equipment or materials this week

request.question: How should I handle the changing particle sizes and choose a useful first approach for the mat with what I already have? Please suggest a concrete next step and what the wet-grip and cleaning goals require.

response.answer:
Separate the granules into a coarse-rich pile and a fine-rich pile and keep them separate. Lay each as a thin, contained patch with the same footprint using only containers or bases you already own, then pour the same amount of cool water through each to compare how water passes and how readily loose dirt rinses out. This keeps variation visible and gives a direct side-by-side on drainage behaviour and rinsing effort.

For your goals, wet grip needs instrumented pendulum assessment by a trained operator under wet conditions for this mat and placement. Rinse comparison can guide layout choice while that assessment is unavailable.
next_steps: Separate remaining granules into coarse-rich and fine-rich portions and keep them labelled.
Make two same-footprint contained patches with existing holders and compare the same cool-water rinse for flow-through and retained dirt.
Seek access to pendulum slip assessment for the wet entry installation.
questions: What shallow trays, old mat bases, or fabric pockets do you already have to hold loose granules without buying anything?
What does easy cleaning need to handle — cool-water rinse only, shaking, limits on particle loss?
What floor surface and wetting will the mat sit on for the slip assessment setup?

sources.title: HSE — assessing floor slip resistance
sources.scope: General floor-slip testing guidance, including instrumented pendulum assessment by a suitably trained operator under relevant surface conditions. It supplies no measured slip value, acceptance target or qualification for the user's recycled material, and no home walking test substitutes for it. Check the current applicable method for the product and installation.
